question: A circle of radius 5 cm and the length of tangent drawn from a point X outside the circle is 12 cm. The distance of the point x from the centre of the circle is :
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A tangent forms a 90° angle with the circle's radius at the point of contact.

The distance from the centre acts as the hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle formed.

Distance from centre = √(Radius² + Tangent²)

Distance = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = 13 cm.

*(Note: 5, 12, 13 is a direct standard Pythagorean triplet, saving calculation time)*

**∴ The correct answer is 13 cm.**
